title: Cells and Cell Division
seo_title: Grade 10 Science (SNC2D): Cells and Cell Division Worksheets (Ontario)
standard_text: Animal and plant cell structure and the functions of organelles; the cell cycle and mitosis; the importance of cell division for growth and repair; cancer as uncontrolled cell division; stem cells and cell specialization; and using a microscope. (summary of The Ontario Curriculum, Grades 9 and 10: Science (2008), Science, Grade 10, Academic (SNC2D), Strand B: Tissues, Organs, and Systems of Living Things)
meta_desc: Free Grade 10 Science (SNC2D) worksheets on cells and cell division: organelles, microscopes and magnification, the cell cycle, the stages of mitosis, cancer and stem cells. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Mitosis makes two identical cells for growth and repair.
key_sub: Prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase, then cytokinesis.
body_html:
How to think about it

Animal and plant cells both have a nucleus (DNA), cytoplasm, a cell membrane, mitochondria (respiration) and ribosomes. Plant cells also have a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large central vacuole. Magnification = image size ÷ actual size.

In the cell cycle, the cell grows and copies its DNA in interphase, then divides in mitosis: prophase (chromosomes condense), metaphase (they line up), anaphase (chromatids separate), telophase (two nuclei form), followed by cytokinesis. Cancer is cell division that is no longer controlled. Stem cells are unspecialized cells that can become many kinds of cells.

Example

A cell is 0.02 mm across. Its image is 10 mm. Magnification?

10 ÷ 0.02

Answer: ×500

Example

In which stage do chromosomes line up across the middle?

Think 'M' for middle.

Answer: metaphase

Common mistakes

  • Saying mitosis halves the chromosome number: it keeps it the same.
  • Forgetting that plant cells also have mitochondria.
  • Mixing up the cell membrane and the cell wall.

faq.q: Why is the cell cycle checked at checkpoints?
faq.a: So that damaged DNA is repaired or the cell is destroyed before it divides; failures can lead to cancer.

items.q: A stem cell in the brain becomes a neuron. Which process is this mainly?
